blurb: Snap's run began after its December 21, 2018 low, helped by user growth returning after the app redesign. On April 23, 2019 it reported 190 million daily active users, up from 186 million in the prior quarter, and revenue up 39% to $320 million; shares rose about 8% to 10% after hours. The stock set its first new 52-week high on June 13, 2019, and peaked in December 2020.

blurb: Vipshop's run is best tied to its August 14, 2019 second-quarter report, which came before its September 10, 2019 first new 52-week high. Total orders rose 33% to 147.8 million, and adjusted net income rose 84% to RMB1.1 billion, though revenue grew only 9.7%. The ADRs rose roughly 15% the next session. The stock had bottomed on October 29, 2018, and peaked in December 2020.

blurb: The Trade Desk's run took off with its fourth-quarter 2018 report on February 21, 2019, after a December 24, 2018 low. Revenue grew 56% to $160.5 million, accelerating from 49.6% the prior quarter and well above the 43% management had forecast. Full-year 2019 revenue guidance of at least $637 million topped consensus. The stock rose 31% on February 22, after a first new 52-week high on February 15.

blurb: GDS bottomed on January 3, 2019, and the March 13, 2019 fourth-quarter report supported the recovery. Full-year 2018 net revenue grew 72.8% to RMB2.79 billion, area in service rose 58.4%, and area under construction rose to 65,201 square meters with a 48.4% pre-commitment rate. The stock made a new 52-week high on July 30, 2019 and peaked in November 2020.

blurb: Zoom listed on April 18, 2019 and based until a low on October 22, 2019. Its breakout to new highs came February 19, 2020, as coronavirus-related remote-work demand lifted the stock about 37% in February. On March 4, 2020 it reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue up 78% to $188.3 million, adjusted EPS of $0.15 versus $0.07 expected, and fiscal 2021 revenue guidance of $905 million to $915 million. It peaked in October 2020.

The stock bottomed August 23, 2019 and broke out September 25. The record shows no single earnings catalyst in my sources; the later run to January 2021 came as residential solar demand strengthened.

The stock made a new high the next day, July 19, and peaked in February 2021.

blurb: Tesla bottomed March 18, 2020. The run was fueled by production holding up and profitability: it earned a $104 million GAAP profit in the second quarter, its fourth straight profitable quarter, which made it eligible for S&P 500 inclusion, even though Fremont was closed from March 23 to May 11. Revenue fell 4.9% to $6.04 billion, and regulatory credits were a large part of profit. Shares neared $1,600 before that report and peaked November 2021.

blurb: Sunrun bottomed March 20, 2020, and jumped 38.9% in April after an April 6 update showing 97.4 megawatts deployed and $366 million of cash. On May 6 it reported first-quarter revenue up 8% to $210.7 million with creation cost per watt down 11% to $3.09. The stock made a new 52-week high July 7, and later gains drew on expectations of a Biden win and clean-energy policy; it peaked January 2021.

blurb: Redfin bottomed March 18, 2020 and made a new high June 3 as housing demand recovered from the pandemic shutdown. Its May 7 report showed first-quarter revenue up 73% to $191 million, above the $183 million expected. Management said seasonally adjusted homebuying demand was back to 96% of its January-February level by May 3, and RedfinNow would resume making offers in May. The stock peaked in February 2021.

blurb: Peloton bottomed March 12, 2020 as stay-at-home orders boosted demand for home fitness. On May 6 it reported fiscal third-quarter revenue up 66% to $524.6 million and connected fitness subscribers up 94% to about 886,000, raised its fiscal 2020 revenue forecast to $1.72 billion to $1.74 billion, and posted its first positive adjusted EBITDA quarter as a public company. It made a new high May 6 and peaked in January 2021.

That report showed COVID-hit results: gross revenue down 21% to $141.8 million, but $4.2 billion of end-to-end volume and a 22% adjusted EBITDA margin on gross revenue less network fees. The stock peaked April 2021.

blurb: GAN listed in May 2020 and, after an October 30, 2020 low, broke out on February 5, 2021, peaking February 16. Its November 2020 deal to buy Coolbet's parent for 149 million euros, closed January 1, 2021, added a sportsbook as US betting expanded. Sources show no clear earnings trigger; full-year 2020 results on March 25, 2021 showed revenue up 17% to $35.2 million, and the stock fell afterward.

blurb: Vertiv bottomed June 30, 2022 and made its first new 52-week high on February 23, 2023, the day after its fourth-quarter report. Organic sales rose 22%, year-end backlog reached a record $4.75 billion (up 49%) and covered over 70% of 2023 sales guidance, and 2023 operating profit guidance was raised. Orders fell 15% in the quarter against a tough comparison. Demand tied to data centers kept the stock rising to October 2024.

blurb: Rambus bottomed July 1, 2022 and set a new 52-week high on November 3, after its October 31 third-quarter report. Product revenue hit a record $58.6 million, up 60% from a year earlier, led by memory interface chips, total GAAP revenue was $112.2 million, and it started a $100 million accelerated share repurchase. Management expected DDR5 ramp to be lumpy, with the DDR4-to-DDR5 server crossover in the first half of 2024. The stock peaked January 2024.

blurb: DraftKings bottomed May 11, 2022 and made its first new 52-week high on April 18, 2023. On May 4, 2023 it reported first-quarter revenue up 84% to $770 million and raised 2023 revenue guidance to $3.135 billion to $3.235 billion from $2.85 billion to $3.05 billion, with adjusted EBITDA losses narrowed and adjusted breakeven expected in the second quarter. Improving losses at a growing sportsbook drove the run to March 2024.

blurb: MongoDB bottomed November 9, 2022 and made a new 52-week high on June 5, 2023, after a blowout report on June 1. First-quarter revenue rose 29% to $368.3 million, Atlas revenue rose 40%, and guidance for the next quarter ($388 million to $392 million) was far above the roughly $362 million analysts expected. The stock rose as much as 35% on June 2 as the company tied results to AI-driven software demand; it peaked in February 2024.
